title: Unified Inference \u2014 Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing (v3)
author: Marina Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates the product overview, high-level PRD, design specs, roadmap and themes, pricing & packaging notes, and release notes for Unified Inference v3. Intended audience: Product, Engineering, Solutions, SRE, Sales.

Summary: Unified Inference v3 is a platform release focused on multi 1tier routing, cost 1aware fallbacks, and simplified pricing for self 1serve customers. The release prioritizes production reliability (SLOs), predictable unit economics, and an opinionated defaults surface to reduce TCO for typical web/mobile LLM use cases.

---

1) Product overview

Goals:
- Provide a single API and control-plane that routes requests across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with consistent semantics.
- Reduce average per 1token cost by 18 30% for enterprise LLM workloads through smarter routing, caching, and quantization recommendations.
- Improve p95 request latency SLA to <= 450ms for 1k-token requests on Hosted Standard tier.

Key capabilities in v3:
- Smart routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, region-aware, and customer-tier policies.
- Model variants and graceful fallbacks: automatic downgrade to quantized or smaller models when capacity throttles.
- Batching and prefix/KV cache auto 1tuning with workload profiles.
- Simplified pricing tiers: Developer (pay-as-you-go), Team (monthly commits), Enterprise (dedicated + SLAs).
- Native support for structured tool-calling and streaming responses.

Stakeholders and owners:
- Product lead: Marina Patel (product)
- Engineering lead: Ethan Chen (eng-serving-runtime)
- Platform owner: Priya Nambiar (eng-platform)
- SRE / Reliability: Liam O'Connor (eng-sre)

---

2) PRD and Requirements (High-level)

Scope: Features targeted for v3 release window (Q3 2026 GA).

Must-have requirements (MUST):
1. Policy-driven smart routing (MUST)
   - Expose routing policy config via API/Console (latency/cost/region/customer-tier)
   - Default policy for new customers: latency-first with cost-awareness threshold = 1.2x baseline
2. Graceful fallback system (MUST)
   - Automatic downgrade fallback path when chosen model exceeds capacity or error rate > 2%
   - Fallbacks to compatible model variants (quantized, smaller architecture) without semantic breakage
3. Autosuggest quantization/profile recommendations (MUST)
   - Provide per-customer profile with recommended quantization + expected cost/latency delta
4. Pricing tier consolidation (MUST)
   - Publish Developer, Team, Enterprise tiers with clear unit economics and commit options
5. SLOs and telemetry (MUST)
   - p50/p95/p99 latency, per-token cost, error rate, and availability metrics available in Console

Should-have requirements (SHOULD):
- First-class SDK updates for streaming and tool calling (SHOULD)
- Built-in prompt/eval templates for canary/quality guards (SHOULD)
- Per-route cost estimates and per-route token quotas (SHOULD)

Out-of-scope (for v3):
- On-prem packaging changes beyond existing Private deployment tooling
- New model family onboarding (will be v4 activity)

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end tests exercising routing policies and fallback paths with simulated capacity failures
- Console displays per-route p95 latency and a cost delta heatmap
- Pricing page updated, billing test performed with simulated commits
- Documentation updated: API reference, SDK guides, and quickstarts

---

3) Design specifications (implementation notes)

Architecture sketch:
- Control plane: routing controller service (route-manager) that evaluates policy graph and issues execution decisions to runtime shards.
- Runtime: serving instances (in-host) with model-variant registry and KV cache metadata.
- Metrics pipeline: event stream tagging for route_id, model_variant, fallback_reason, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out.

API surface (examples)
- Route policy create API (JSON):
```
POST /v1/routes
{
  "name": "team-default",
  "policy": {
    "priority": ["latency","cost"],
    "region_preference": ["us-west-2","us-east-1"],
    "fallback_budget_multiplier": 1.2
  }
}
```
- Inference request example with tool-calling and streaming:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-unified-7b",
  "prompt": "Summarize the quarterly metrics",
  "stream": true,
  "tools": [{"name":"sql-query","schema":"..."}]
}
```

Model variant registry table (example, described in text):
- Columns: variant_id | base_model | quantization | expected_p95_ms | cost_multiplier | compatible_with
- Example row: "rv-7b-q4" | "redwood-7b" | "4-bit-ptq" | "320" | "0.45" | "redwood-7b,redwood-7b-compat"

Fallback decision flow (numbered):
1. Route-manager evaluates policy on request arrival.
2. If preferred model has no capacity or error rate > 2% over 1 minute, mark as degraded.
3. Consult variant registry for compatible variants sorted by cost_multiplier ascending.
4. Attempt variant with acceptable latency delta <= policy.fallback_budget_multiplier * baseline_latency.
5. Emit event fallback_event with reason and variant chosen.

Operational runbooks (high level):
- Canary rollout steps: 1) Enable route policy in internal sandbox, 2) Run 24h quality eval set, 3) Gradual traffic ramp 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 48 372h, 4) Monitor quality regressions and fallback events.
- Rollback criteria: increase in fallback rate > 5% absolute or quality regression > 3% on eval set.

Security considerations:
- Model metadata and routing decisions are considered customer-metadata; ensure RBAC enforcement on route APIs (console + API).
- Audit logs for all policy changes kept for 365 days; events forwarded to SIEM.

---

4) Roadmap & themes (Q3 2026 \u2014 Q2 2027)

Themes by quarter:
- Q3 2026 (v3 GA): Smart routing, fallbacks, pricing consolidation, console telemetry
- Q4 2026: Dedicated autoscaling policies, advanced caching (cross-request), SLA beta for Enterprise
- Q1 2027: Private deployment synchronization, advanced model compaction tools, SDK parity
- Q2 2027: Multi-region active-active, marketplace model variants, partner integrations

Milestones and dates:
- 2026-08-10: PRD finalized (this doc)
- 2026-08-22: Design review and API freeze
- 2026-09-01: Internal canary start (sandbox)
- 2026-09-08: External beta with select customers
- 2026-09-15: GA release (v3) and public pricing page update

KPIs to measure success (owner in parentheses):
- Platform p95 latency reduction vs v2 (Ethan Chen) \u2014 target: -15%
- Average per-token cost for Team tier (Finance/Product) \u2014 target: -20%
- Customer onboarding time (support -> first successful call) (Solutions) \u2014 target: <1 day for self-serve
- Fallback rate in production (SRE) \u2014 target: <2% after 30 days

---

5) Pricing & packaging notes

Summary of pricing tiers (public):
- Developer (Pay-as-you-go): Per-token billing, free 10k token monthly credit, baseline model catalog, streaming included.
  - Example rates (approximate): text-generation $0.0004 / 1k tokens baseline (unified-7b), embeddings $0.0006 / 1k vectors.
- Team (Committed monthly): Discounted unit costs with burstable capacity and route-level quotas. Commit tiers: $2K/month, $10K/month, $50K/month.
  - Team bundle includes a set of 3 reserved concurrency units and 30-day billing reconciliation.
- Enterprise (Reserved + Private): Custom pricing for Dedicated/Private. SLA: 99.95% uptime (hosted) for reserved pools, on-prem support packages available.

Cost controls & packaging features:
- Per-route quotas and alerts
- Autosuggested quantization profiles with expected monthly savings shown in Console
- Monthly commit reconciliation and overage handling: 10% buffer grace, then overage at published pay-as-you-go rates

Billing and legal notes:
- All public pricing listed on pricing.redwood.ai and in Console billing page.
- Contracts for Team and Enterprise include service credits for missed SLAs and standard data handling addenda (DPA).

---

6) Release notes (v3 GA \u2014 2026-09-15)

Highlights:
- Smart routing policies (latency-first, cost-first, region-aware) introduced
- Automatic graceful fallback to model variants when capacity or quality degrades
- Console improvements: per-route latency & cost heatmaps, quantization recommendation panel
- Pricing updated: consolidated Developer/Team/Enterprise tiers and example rates published

Behavior changes and compatibility:
- Default routing policy for all existing orgs will remain unchanged for 30 days post 1GA; orgs will receive an opt-in prompt to enable new policy defaults.
- Model-variant naming introduces a short alias (rv-7b-q4). Backwards compatibility: inference API accepts either base model or variant alias.

Known issues (short list):
- Some legacy SDK clients may not surface streaming improvements; SDK updates are scheduled across v3.x patches. (tracked: #ENG-SDK-214)
- Under high fanout, fallback_event rate may briefly spike while runtime shards rebalance (mitigation: 2-minute cooldown on route-manager decisions).

Changelog (high level):
- 2026-09-08: Beta release to select customers.
- 2026-09-15: GA release and public pricing update.

---

7) Rollout plan and runbook (concise)

Canary checklist:
- QA verifies routing policy APIs and fallback metrics in sandbox
- Run eval set (1.2k prompts) looking for quality regressions > 2%
- Confirm telemetry emits route_id, model_variant, fallback_reason, tokens_in/out, and latency_ms

Traffic ramping plan:
1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 72 hours with checkpoints at 24h intervals.
Monitoring thresholds (automatic rollback triggers):
- Fallback rate increase > 5% absolute over baseline
- p95 latency breach of SLA by > 20% for 30 minutes
- Quality regression > 3% on eval set during canary window

Post-release tasks (30 days):
- Weekly quality review for early adopters and top 10 Team customers
- Billing reconciliation with any customers who used beta commits
- SDK / quickstart updates and communication campaign (Docs + Blog + Developer newsletter)

---

8) Documentation & Enablement

Deliverables before GA:
- API reference: routing policy endpoints, generate endpoints, model-variant registry docs
- SDK releases: JS, Python updates with streaming/tool calling examples
- Console walkthrough and quickstarts: Creating a route, enabling fallback, viewing cost estimates
- Sales enablement: one-pager, slide deck, and pricing FAQ

---

9) Risks & mitigation

Top risks:
- Unexpected quality regressions when falling back to quantized variants (mitigation: conservative fallback_budget_multiplier, pre-prod eval sets)
- Customer confusion about new pricing tiers (mitigation: clear migration FAQs and account manager outreach for Team/Enterprise)
- Operational complexity in route-manager (mitigation: feature flags, circuit-breakers, and robust telemetry)

Open items:
- Finalize Team commit discount bands and overage grace policy (action: Finance + Product, due 2026-08-20)
- Confirm internal SLA reporting cadence and service credit formula (action: Legal + SRE, due 2026-08-25)
